# Marko Stankovic

> AI engineer based in Serbia, open to remote or EU roles. He builds agent
> systems and the tools that measure whether they actually worked: headless
> agent loops that ship reviewed code, evaluation harnesses for LLM behaviour,
> and gates that fail loudly instead of passing quietly. Primary languages
> Python, TypeScript and C#.

Marko works AI-first: agents are the primary tool, not autocomplete. He runs a
personal AI operating system of roughly forty skills, path scoped rules, and an
overnight loop that selects an unblocked issue, implements it test first, passes
a review gate, and records a real commit. The recurring theme across his public
work is measurement: most teams ship AI features they cannot check, and he
builds the instruments that check them, including the instruments' own limits.

Underneath that sits three years of Unity and Unreal Engine systems work in C#
and C++, plus full-stack TypeScript on Next.js. He works CLI-first on Arch Linux.

## Skills
- Agent orchestration: headless Claude Code loops, sub-agent review gates, tool design
- LLM evaluation: judge calibration, regression evals on golden sets, decay probes
- Python, primary language for tooling and synthesis engines
- TypeScript, Node and Next.js, full-stack product work
- C#, three years in Unity; C++ in Unreal Engine 5
- Automation and developer tooling, CLI design, CI gates

## Projects
- [adpreflight](https://github.com/marko-builds/adpreflight): pre-flight validator
  for ad creatives. One command checks a build zip against network rule packs and
  exits non-zero naming the exact rule that failed. Static checks plus a headless
  Chromium assertion. Every limit cites its primary source and retrieval date
  inline, rules are marked cited or derived so a reader can tell which are
  inferred, and a third exit code means "no verdict established" rather than
  letting an unearned pass through. Open source, MIT.
- [skill-vibe-test](https://github.com/marko-builds/skill-vibe-test): measures
  whether a Claude Code skill still steers the model after ten turns of unrelated
  conversation. A scripted conversation in one growing context, an LLM judge
  scoring against a rubric extracted from the skill, and a decay curve as output.
  His own skill failed the probe and he published the result. Open source, MIT.
- [DeployLog](https://deploylog.dev): changelog and release-notes platform that
  turns git commits into a published changelog (hosted page, embeddable widget,
  npm CLI, and a GitHub Action) from one source, with AI-drafted notes. Built
  full-stack on Next.js, Supabase, and Stripe. Status: launching 2026-09-15.
  Details: https://markostankovic.org/projects/deploylog
- [duskpaper](https://github.com/marko-builds/duskpaper): generative animated
  Wayland wallpapers rendered locally at your seed and resolution, from his own
  procedural synthesis engines. Open source.
- Habitagram: habit tracking as a journey. A React Native app where habits move a
  boat across illustrated landscapes that shift with the time of day, with the art
  rendered from code rather than drawn. Private repo, near launch. No public link
  yet.
- [BlenderBridge](https://github.com/marko-builds/BlenderBridge): five manual
  cleanup steps on every Blender-to-Unreal import, cut to one click. A UE5 editor
  plugin that enforces asset naming, fixes normal maps, generates lightmap UVs,
  and runs a pre-flight validation pass. Hybrid build: a thin C++ Slate panel over
  a Python core. Open source, v0.1.
